note: Frozen exceptions to the accuracy policy (see fork-notes/accuracy-policy.md). Each entry matches one scanner finding by path, category, match and line fingerprint; line_at_base is informational. An entry whose text is gone is stale and must be deleted.

A1.summary: Title-keyed preset tables, recommendation prompts and per-title tweak screens
A1.removal: Delete the tables, prompts and tweak screens; defaults come from the console model and settings stay global.

A2.summary: Title-gated main-module patch rewriting frame-interval accounting, with fixed and dynamic frame-rate settings
A2.removal: Delete when frame pacing follows the intervals the guest presents through a console display model; remove both settings.

A3.summary: Title-gated module patch writing frame-interval globals, with a controller using fixed thresholds
A3.removal: Delete with A2; no recorded addresses or guest memory writes may remain.

A4.summary: Built-in frame-rate patch matched by build prefix and byte offset
A4.removal: Delete; frame rate is not a patch and no build prefix may select behaviour.

A5.summary: Built-in patch matched by build id and offset that bypasses a dynamic-resolution floor
A5.removal: Delete the patch-table entry; resolution selection stays guest-controlled.

A6.summary: Built-in time-step hook matched by build id, deriving simulation steps from host frame time
A6.removal: Delete; guest time must come only from the modelled console clocks.

A7.summary: Program-id override forcing squashed iterated blending
A7.removal: Replace with the correct blend-state model for every title; delete the override entry and setting.

A8.summary: Depth-bias scale applied for a list of program ids when the guest depth format is missing on the host
A8.removal: Derive the scale from the guest/host format pair for every title; delete the id list.

A9.summary: Missing-firmware warning shown for one program id
A9.removal: Delete, or make the warning depend on firmware presence for every title.

B1.summary: Frames-ahead fence choice forced by program id, with fence-wait knobs and escapes
B1.removal: Replace with one ordering rule justified by console queue semantics; delete the id test and knobs.

B2.summary: Legacy timestamp path kept for one program id
B2.removal: Delete after the generic timestamp path is shown correct for it.

B3.summary: Movie pacing bypass for one program id above a width threshold
B3.removal: Delete; pacing must follow the presented intervals, not a title.

B4.summary: Decoded-frame time window that defeats a forced swap interval
B4.removal: Replace with a rule derived from the media clock or delete.

B5.summary: Crop of one allocation size to a fixed size for docked mode
B5.removal: Use the shown-size metadata for every title; delete the special size.

B6.summary: Video decode pacing guesses and drop thresholds
B6.removal: Replace with pacing from the actual media clock; delete the thresholds.

B7.summary: Decoder end-of-stream release workaround (default off) and handoff fence rules
B7.removal: Replace with the specified lifecycle semantics; delete the knob.

B8.summary: Pushbuffer snapshot policy and mapping deferral
B8.removal: Keep only if justified by the console command-submission model; remove title comments.

B9.summary: Idle spin default for the emulated CPU cores
B9.removal: Host scheduling policy; remove title comments and keep a global default.

B10.summary: Host pause inserted on closely spaced counter reads
B10.removal: Host policy; remove title comments and keep a global default.

B11.summary: StartThread waiting loop with fixed sleeps
B11.removal: Replace with a scheduling rule from kernel semantics or delete.

B12.summary: Minimum host delay on HLE IPC replies
B12.removal: Replace with a scheduling rule from kernel semantics or delete.

B13.summary: Storage read throttle at fixed rates
B13.removal: Replace with a storage timing model or delete; no title tuning.

B14.summary: Fixed sleeps in legacy builds on first video decoder and image processor creation

C1.summary: Tensor lowering permitted for specific networks, with compile-time motivation
C1.removal: Replace with capability-based lowering; delete the network-specific permission.

C2.summary: Host DLSS interception keyed by hashed inputs and outputs with fixed buffer layouts
C2.removal: Delete the interception; host enhancement must not recognise a title.

C3.summary: Movie path recognised by an image-read layout, with an upscale replacement window
C3.removal: Delete or replace with an opcode-level rule.

C4.summary: Network chain tracking using fixed constant-buffer offsets
C4.removal: Delete; treat library ABI through a documented interface only.

C5.summary: Upscale stand-in recognising fixed slots, dimensions and instruction constants
C5.removal: Delete the stand-in recognition; keep only host enhancement.

C6.summary: Depth-scene copy for one program id at one width

C7.summary: Shader patch keyed by a shader hash, size and location
C7.removal: Delete the patch; fix the underlying cause generally.

C8.summary: Eager publication of a texture keyed by a native hash and constant-buffer layout

C9.summary: Pipeline-cache subdirectory chosen for one program id
C9.removal: Replace with a global cache namespace version.

C10.summary: CPU rewrite of indirect reset records for one shader key

C11.summary: Driver compile policy by shader hash
C11.removal: Replace with a driver workload policy independent of shader identity.

C12.removal: Delete or keep as a debugging tool that cannot ship per-title data.

C13.summary: Undefined shader outputs defaulted to zero
C13.removal: Replace with the specified register reset state.

C14.removal: Keep only if shown lossless; remove title comments.

C15.summary: Vendor driver workaround rewriting a shifted add pattern
C15.removal: Keep only as a structural, title-free rule; remove title comments.

C16.summary: Descriptor-array bound inferred from a found-bit pattern
C16.removal: Keep as a pattern rule; remove title comments.

C17.removal: Replace with a derivation from the texture header or delete.

C18.summary: Silent drop of a copy with incompatible bytes per block on Windows
C18.removal: Replace with a real conversion path.

C19.removal: Host cache policy; remove title comments.

C20.summary: Texture cache budgets and garbage collection
C20.removal: Host capacity policy; remove title comments.

C21.summary: ASTC recompression defaults and budget override
C21.removal: Host capacity policy; remove title comments.

C22.summary: Buffer cache preflush marks and aging
C22.removal: Host coherence policy; remove title comments.

C23.summary: ASTC array trimming and sparse image backing caps
C23.removal: Replace with a lossless capacity policy; remove title comments.

C24.removal: Host enhancement setting; remove title comments.

C25.summary: Bloom-fix setting and its sampling changes
C25.removal: Replace with a correct sampling model; delete the setting.

C26.removal: Model the shading-state register; delete the forced result.

C27.summary: Constant-bank remap and synthetic values for a fullscreen blit

C28.removal: Use the hardware reset register image; delete the per-title notes.

C29.summary: Atomic operation decode ordering note naming a title
C29.removal: Establish the encoding; remove the note.

C30.summary: Macro hash to HLE implementation table and JIT capacity note
C30.removal: Prove each substitution by byte and behaviour equivalence; remove title notes.

C31.summary: Geometry output pruning from consumer reads
C31.removal: Keep when proven; remove title comments.

D1.summary: Address-space and memory-pool sizing for the newer console model

D3.summary: Sparse and GPU-only region backing and remap policy
D3.removal: Replace with the specified mapping semantics.

D4.summary: Placeholder sessions and automatic command success for missing services
D4.removal: Implement each service; delete the blanket stub.

D5.summary: GPU capability bits and characteristic block advertised for title needs

D6.removal: Replace with protocol-version parsing; delete forced encoding and fallback.

D7.summary: Audio device-change event commands answered with an empty valid handle

D8.summary: Vibration command accepted and dropped until its layout is known

D9.summary: Web applet early return for one initial mode

D10.summary: Friend service commands returning success without state

D11.summary: Hostname-substring denylist in the DNS resolver
D11.removal: Security and network policy; remove title comments only.

D12.summary: Network availability counted from a joined room
D12.removal: Host transport policy; remove title comments.

D13.removal: Make add-on enumeration general; delete the switch.

D14.summary: Duplicate program entry precedence in content packages

D15.summary: Decoder factory variants and pool layout assumptions

D17.removal: Validate counter wrap and re-arm; remove title comments.

D18.summary: Native window placement, header-bit tiling and rectangle metadata rules
D18.removal: Keep as general format rules; remove title comments.

M1.summary: Program, title or build id used as storage, content-registry, save, play-time or access identity
M1.removal: Kept while the use is identity, not behaviour. A use that selects emulation behaviour is a violation, not an exception.

M2.summary: Game-list display metadata: icon aliases keyed by title id
M2.removal: Delete when the aliases move to a lab or user-data artefact.

M3.summary: Lab, automation and issue-reporting artefacts that name tested games or captured hashes
M3.removal: Move out of the emulator repository or delete.

M4.summary: Instruction encodings, hash-function constants and test vectors that resemble identities
M4.removal: Delete the entry only if the literal is removed; these are not identities.

T1.summary: Test fixtures that name or encode a listed exception
T1.removal: Delete with the exception they test, or rewrite with neutral fixtures.

U1.summary: Found by this check but not in the plan inventory
U1.removal: Review: remove the branch, or add an inventory record with a proof that it is not per-game.
